abstract: Adoptive transfer experiments (e.g. hematopoietic stem cell transplantation) are indispensable for hematology and immunology research. These assays require unambiguous detection of the transferred cells, and their offspring, to track their fates. Mice in which a fluorescent reporter protein is expressed ubiquitously in all cells are especially helpful for these fate mapping experiments as the donor cells can be easily detected using flow cytometry and confocal microscopy. We report that two commonly used reporter strains, Ubc-gfp and ROSA-mTmG, display variable expression during hematopoietic differentiation. GFP in Ubc-gfp mice labels only a fraction of megakaryocytes while TdTomato expression in ROSA-mTmG mice is progressively lost in red blood cells. We also found uneven expression of either reporter at various stages of B cell, myeloid cell or dendritic cell differentiation. Our results thus enable selection of the appropriate fluorescent reporter for identification of the hematopoietic cells of interest in adoptive transfer experiments.
